candidate_sentence_map.S1: During the 2025 financial year, TKM Grupp AS experienced a weakening of financial performance amid a challenging economic environment characterized by low consumer confidence, high price sensitivity, and domestic tax changes in Estonia, notably the introduction of a motor vehicle tax.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Consolidated sales revenue declined by 2.6 percent to 919.6 million euros compared to 944.6 million euros in the previous year.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Profitability contracted more significantly, with profit before tax falling by 31.4 percent to 24.3 million euros and net profit decreasing by 36.1 percent to 17.5 million euros.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Net profit per share dropped to 43 cents from 67 cents.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Effective cost control helped mitigate pressures from rising expenses, while net profit also benefited from lower borrowing interest costs.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Performance varied across the Group's segments.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: The supermarkets segment generated revenue of 611.9 million euros, a modest increase of 0.3 percent, while net profit declined by 38.6 percent to 9.5 million euros due to a higher share of promotional products and lower consumer purchasing power.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: The department stores segment saw revenue decrease by 1.1 percent to 103.0 million euros, resulting in a net loss of 0.5 million euros.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: The car trade segment was severely impacted, with revenue dropping by 11.9 percent to 176.9 million euros and net profit falling by 54.4 percent to 4.3 million euros, driven by a sharp contraction in the Estonian passenger car market following the motor vehicle tax introduction.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: This domestic weakness was partially cushioned by stable operations in Latvian and Lithuanian subsidiaries.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The security segment reported external revenue of 20.1 million euros, an 8.1 percent decrease, with net profit at zero.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: Conversely, the real estate segment increased external revenue by 5.1 percent to 7.7 million euros, supported by rental income from a new logistics centre, and net profit rose to 6.3 million euros despite the comparative period including one-off property sale gains and revaluations.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Total investments during 2025 amounted to 25.5 million euros, down from 36.6 million euros in 2024, directed toward store refurbishments, digital upgrades, and a new car centre in Vilnius.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Cash and cash equivalents decreased from 45.5 million euros to 29.5 million euros at year-end, and working capital was negative at 14.1 million euros due to the classification of long-term loans maturing in 2026, totaling 32.1 million euros, as current liabilities ahead of planned refinancing.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: In January 2026, the Group agreed to acquire additional vehicle retail companies in Estonia to expand its car segment operations.
